# SexOS hardware compatibility list

<!-- Generated by scripts/hardware_list.py from crates/sex-hwdb and hw-reports/. Do not edit by hand. -->

What SexOS drives today, device by device, and what real machines have shown. Two sources feed it, and nothing in it is written by hand:

- **Support** is what the driver table in `crates/sex-hwdb` says about master: the same table BOOT prints as `[hw.device]` lines on every boot.
- **Seen on** is what real machines reported: each machine's newest Spindle `hw save` report under `hw-reports/` (see its README to send one). `works` means the driver came up on that machine; `failed` means it was there and did not.

Any device not named below falls under the class rules at the end. To add a device, add its row to `crates/sex-hwdb`; to write its driver, start from the driver SDK (`docs/sdk/DRIVER_SDK.md`).

70 named devices, 43 of them working on master. 0 real machines reported.

## Support levels

| Support | Meaning |
|---|---|
| driven | Works: a SexOS driver drives it |
| firmware | Works through firmware setup only (boot framebuffer), no native driver yet |
| platform | Platform plumbing; nothing to drive |
| in_progress | Driver in progress (open branch or untried on real hardware) |
| planned | In the driver plan, not started |
| none | Not supported |

## Real machines

No real-machine report yet. The first will come from the Alienware x17 R1 (`docs/handoff/X17_BARE_METAL_RUNBOOK_2026_11_18.md`).
